item.text: {"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"During 2023, Sisi-linked formal initiatives addressed regional crises, but the supplied evidence shows limited demonstrated advancement beyond initiating mechanisms. The presidency records Sisi’s agreement to resume GERD negotiations with a four-month target and Egypt’s convening of mechanisms concerning Sudan, while later reporting found no worthwhile progress in the dam talks and does not document implementation of the Sudan mechanism (BATCH-0016-E004; BATCH-0016-E007; BATCH-0021-E012). In Gaza, presidential diplomacy sought civilian protection, humanitarian access, de-escalation, and a two-state solution; Egyptian authorities facilitated initial aid entry, and Egypt accepted patients and coordinated evacuation infrastructure, but the record does not establish sustained access, outcomes, or Sisi’s personal control over ministry, Red Crescent, WHO, or WFP operations (BATCH-0021-E009; BATCH-0015-E004; BATCH-0014-E009; BATCH-0018-E004; BATCH-0019-E007; BATCH-0019-E008; BATCH-0019-E009). Domestic resistance was managed with substantial coercive capacity: authorities detained critics and Palestine-solidarity protesters, while the army used force and military proceedings against North Sinai residents demanding return. This preserved regime control in an operational sense, but the evidence does not establish Sisi’s personal authorization for individual operations, and it documents failure to deliver the promised return of displaced residents (BATCH-0009-R03-E014; BATCH-0009-R03-E015; BATCH-0020-E006; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0022-E011). The 2023 election secured Sisi’s continued tenure through a process that Freedom House describes as eliminating meaningful competition, but that fact alone is not evidence of effective crisis management or progress across his broader objectives (BATCH-0002-E001). Overall, the record supports strong regime-control capacity and some attributable diplomatic initiative, alongside unresolved international objectives, implementation gaps, and coercive responses that diverged from stated inclusion or protest-support
